summary: This note surveys anti-aircraft (air defence) warfare, covering how militaries organise air defence, the historical development of anti-aircraft guns, fire control, sensors and rockets, and the defence against V-1 missiles at Antwerp. It also covers terminology, NATO definitions, passive defence, air defence suppression, and layered naval air defence with carrier groups.
one_line: An overview of anti-aircraft warfare: military organisation, gun and missile development, radar and fire control, V-1 defence, terminology and naval layered defence.
key_facts: The Pakistan Army split air defence off from Artillery to form a separate arm of its own in 1990.
The US ended World War I with two 3-inch AA guns, and work on a 90 mm AA gun followed the 1924 start of a 105 mm static mounting AA gun.
The M1 version of the 90 mm AA gun was approved in 1940.

After the Dambusters raid in 1943, a new system was developed that was required to knock down any low-flying aircraft with a single hit, and a new 55 mm gun replaced an initial 50 mm gun that proved inaccurate.
The Brocq system was a French electrical tachymetric device used with the 75 mm gun, while the British Wilson-Dalby gun director used a pair of trackers and mechanical tachymetry.
The British Anti-Aircraft Command was disbanded in March 1955, and all ground-based air defence was removed from RAF jurisdiction in 2004.
The term air defence was probably first used by Britain when Air Defence of Great Britain (ADGB) was created as a Royal Air Force command in 1925.
During the Antwerp X project, close to 90% of the V-1 missiles on track to the defence zone around the port were destroyed, using SCR-584 radar, the M-9 director and radio proximity fuses.
The smallest tactical unit of the Antwerp X operation was a gun battery of four 90 mm guns firing shells with a radio proximity fuse.
The Nike Ajax missile was used in a US upgrade of its defences, after which the larger anti-aircraft guns soon disappeared.
At its peak in 1941–42, the UK's Anti-Aircraft Command comprised three AA corps with 12 AA divisions between them.
NATO defines anti-aircraft warfare (AAW) as measures taken to defend a maritime force against attacks by airborne weapons launched from aircraft, ships, submarines and land-based sites.
The nickname 'archie' was a World War I British term probably coined by Amyas Borton, believed to derive from George Robey's music-hall line "Archibald, certainly not!".
The Soviet PVO Strany, the Strategic Air defence Service for Air Defence of the Homeland, was created in 1941 and became an independent service in 1954.
In naval layered defence, the RIM-67 Standard has a range of up to 100 nmi and the RIM-162 ESSM has a range of up to 30 nmi; a CIWS is usually a radar-controlled Gatling gun of 20mm to 30mm calibre.

entities.role: has air defence as part of its artillery arm

entities.role: British Army command disbanded in March 1955 that was part of ADGB

entities.name: RAF Regiment
entities.role: formed in World War II to protect airfields everywhere, including with light air defences

entities.name: Royal Marines
entities.role: provided air defence units during World War II as part of mobile naval base defence

entities.name: Observer Corps
entities.role: volunteer body formed in 1925 providing observation posts to report hostile aircraft over Britain

entities.name: 419th and 601st Antiaircraft Gun Battalions
entities.role: US Army units allocated to the Folkestone-Dover coast, then moved to Belgium for the Antwerp X project

entities.name: Antwerp X
entities.role: project defending the port city of Antwerp against V-1 and V-2 missiles

entities.name: SCR-584 radar
entities.role: radar developed at the MIT Rad Lab that automatically tracked incoming targets

entities.name: M-9 director
entities.role: electronic analog computer developed at Bell Laboratories to calculate lead and elevation corrections for guns

entities.name: Brocq system
entities.role: French electrical tachymetric device used with the 75 mm gun

entities.name: Wilson-Dalby gun director
entities.role: British gun director using a pair of trackers and mechanical tachymetry

entities.name: Nike Ajax
entities.role: missile used in the US upgrade of its defences

entities.name: SA-2 Guideline
entities.role: Soviet missile system whose introduction led to the disappearance of larger anti-aircraft guns in the USSR

entities.name: MIM-104 Patriot
entities.role: missile batteries used to defend Saudi Arabia and Israel during the first Gulf War

entities.name: Fliegerfaust
entities.role: unguided German system described as the first MANPADS

entities.name: Wasserfall
entities.role: sophisticated German radio, wire or radar guided missile

entities.name: RIM-162 ESSM
entities.role: point-defence naval missile with a range of up to 30 nmi
